Mountain Brook Municipal Court is a city courthouse in the county of Alabama. The court has jurisdiction over traffic, vehicle, and criminal and small claims matters. Its division gives administrative support to the city government judicial branch, case docketing and management, and caseload reporting. The judges, prosecutors, and staff service ensure comfortable and efficient court service to every person in the court. The court session is held every Wednesday except the fifth Wednesday of the month at 3:00 pm.

How to search for the case record?

Mountain Brook Municipal Court records are available at the court office in files, on the computer, and online. They can be found online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by name
  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Some information about cases is not available online because they are confidential by law. These types of information are only available at the court office. You had to submit a form for this information by visiting the court, and then the court would respond whether to provide the record information or not. Mostly confidential information is only given to the person involved in the case or to the police or investigation agency. The record search request is free of cost.

What is the method of paying a traffic ticket online?

Mountain Brook Municipal Court pay online can be done by using mountainbrookpayments.com. After clicking it, the payment portal is opened. The portal had five steps: lookup, info, amount, payment, and receipt. You can look up the case using citation number, case number, or by last name and date of birth. After filling in all the information and paying, the fine receipt will be generated.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

zMountain Brook Municipal Court Traffic Court handles cases of traffic and vehicle violations. The violation includes speeding, accidents, using cell phones while driving, failing to follow a traffic signal or traffic control device, driving while intoxicated, with a suspended or no license, leaving the scene of the accident, and driving recklessly. You can send a guilty or not guilty plea to the court before the date written on the ticket you received. The court will respond with whether to appear in court for the case, or only fines will be paid. Your driving license and driving privileges will be suspended if you do not pay the fine on time. You cannot request your license renewal until the court approves. The Police Department of the Town gives the speeding ticket. Hire a professional traffic Ticket attorney for traffic and speeding cases because they can defend you against the traffic charges in court.

How to make payments?

Mountain Brook Municipal Court pay the ticket, and other fines can be made in the following ways:

· In-Person:

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter. Convenience and other charges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

· Online:

A person can pay online using the online payment link mountainbrookpayments.com.Fill all the information and pay with any online method. Service fees of a minimum of $3 or 4% will be applied per transaction in this online method.

· Mail:

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address. The address is 56 Church St, Mountain Brook, AL 35213, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted.

· Phone:

Payment can also be made using the phone by calling 1-205-619-1545

What are the fees for a traffic ticket?

Mountain Brook Municipal Court traffic ticket fees depend upon the violation a person has done. $195 for driving on the wrong side of the road, $185 for improper passing, turning or tinting of the window, $235 if the driver with an expired license, $175 for not dimming headlights, $215 if a person does not have any proof of insurance, $205 for speeding over 25 mph and $225 for Violating driver's license restriction or endorsement etc. Call 1-844-334-4349 if you want any guidance or information.

How will a traffic ticket be dismissed from the record?

Mountain Brook Municipal Court Defensive Driving classes allow ticket dismissal off the records. If the person's age is 19+, then visit the court and check whether you qualify for these classes or not. If the age is below 19, then the judge requires permission. 4 and 8 hours of classes are available, and you can qualify for either one of them; it depends upon your driving history. The cost for 4 hours of driving classes is $100 with $165 court fees and $150with $165 court fees for 8 hours of driving lessons, and this payment can be made during the registration. If you are eligible for the classes, then the magistrate will provide you with all the schedule and location information. You had to take courses in person; online is not allowed.

What is the role of the clerk?

Mountain Brook Municipal Court clerk's role is maintaining each case file, receiving and handling payment and fines, and helping the judge in the case hearing. They are responsible for the maintenance of all Official Town Records and the issuance of various licenses. They are an agent of licensing and custodians of the town records. They provide marriage licenses, birth and death certificates, permits, etc.

Visit the court during regular hours or call and email the clerk.

How can I request for a Driver's License Reinstatement?

Download the document form for the Driver's License Reinstatement request, fill in all the information, and send it to the court.

What is the total cost of allowing a child under 16 to drive a vehicle?

You had to pay $215 if you allowed your child under 16 to drive a vehicle.

What happens if I do not pay the fine on time?

If you do not pay the fine on time, an extra amount will be added to your fine, your driving license or insurance will be suspended, and you cannot renew it until the court gives the order.

What is the dress code of the court?

You should wear proper and respectable clothes. Sleeveless, tight, and torn clothes are not allowed during the hearing.
